t: Walk in Both Reverence and Rejoicing as We Welcome God’s Presence into the Center of Life
v: David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale Judah, to bring up from there God’s ark, which is called by the Name, even the name of the LORD of Armies who sits above the cherubim.
When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached for God’s ark and took hold of it, for the cattle stumbled.
The LORD’s anger burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there for his error; and he died there by God’s ark.
David was displeased because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez Uzzah to this day.
David was afraid of the LORD that day; and he said, “How could the LORD’s ark come to me?”
So David would not move the LORD’s ark to be with him in David’s city; but David carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
The LORD’s ark remained in Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his house.

King David was told, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that belongs to him, because of God’s ark.” So David went and brought up God’s ark from the house of Obed-Edom into David’s city with joy.
When those who bore the LORD’s ark had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.
So David and all the house of Israel brought up the LORD’s ark with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.
b: This history records King David welcoming the ark of God—the symbol of God’s presence—into Jerusalem. But the process did not go as expected. It became a spiritual lesson in “reverence and rejoicing walking together.”

Uzzah put out his hand to steady the ark, seemingly out of instinct to protect it, but he was struck down for violating God’s holiness. This reminds us that God’s presence is glorious and not to be treated lightly. When we long to draw near to God, we must also respond to his holiness with fitting reverence and obedience.

David was at first distressed and afraid of God and did not dare move the ark into the city. But when he heard that God blessed the place where the ark stayed, he understood that the problem was not with God but with whether people honor him in the right way. So he changed his actions and rearranged how the ark was worshiped and carried—this time not by his own ideas, but according to God’s heart.

When reverence is put in its place, God’s blessing comes; when God’s presence is honored, the people are filled with shouts of joy. David, wearing a priestly ephod and setting aside his royal dignity, danced with all his might before everyone, because he knew that all glory belongs to God.
This is the true meaning of worship: not only joy and music, but reverence and offering—responding in spirit and truth to the glorious Lord.
a: Long for God’s presence, but respect God’s holiness
God delights to dwell with people, but we must welcome him with a holy life.
Adjust how we serve and worship
Do not rely only on zeal and habit, but return to the standard and heart found in God’s word.
Let God dwell at the center of life
Do not keep God at the edges, but let his presence direct our thoughts and decisions.
q: Like David, do I long for God’s presence while neglecting reverence? Am I willing to adjust myself so that God has a true dwelling place?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, forgive me for the times I have treated Your presence lightly and put myself at the center. Teach me to serve You with reverence and to welcome You with joy. May my life be more than formal worship, but a true altar that honors You and magnifies You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When You Can’t See Through Life’s Events, Still Fear God and Walk Forward in Peace
v: There is a vanity which is done on the earth, that there are righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked. Again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (even though eyes see no sleep day or night),

then I saw all the work of God, that man can’t find out the work that is done under the sun, because however much a man labors to seek it out, yet he won’t find it. Yes even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he won’t be able to find it.
b: This passage is a deep reflection on life and wisdom by King Solomon in his old age. He observed a phenomenon that is hard to accept: “the righteous experience what the wicked deserve, and the wicked experience what the righteous deserve.” In other words, the way the world works often seems unfair, leaving people confused and helpless.

In our own lives we also see good people suffer and bad people prosper. It can leave us puzzled, even asking, “Is God really just?” Yet Solomon points to a way forward in this observation: even if we can’t see through it, we should not stop fearing God and enjoying the grace he gives.

When he says, “a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, drink, and be joyful,” he is not encouraging indulgence, but reminding us that since life is full of mystery and the unknowable, we should learn thankfulness within our limits and recognize God’s blessing in ordinary things. God does not require that we understand everything before we trust him, but that even when we don’t understand, we still choose to trust and rejoice.

Finally, Solomon admits, “man can’t find out the work of God.” This is humble wisdom. We are not God and cannot understand every mystery, and we do not have to demand answers for everything. True wisdom is not knowing everything, but choosing to fear God and walk forward in peace even in not knowing.
a: Accept that there are many things in life we cannot see through
Do not let unfair appearances shake our trust in God.
Learn thankfulness and joy in everyday life
Enjoying each day God gives is a way of treasuring his grace.
Walk by faith on a path we cannot clearly see
Even when the road ahead is hazy, believe that God reigns and his will is higher than our understanding.
q: When I see the righteous suffer and the wicked profit, what is my attitude? Am I still willing to believe in God’s justice and wisdom?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, when I face things in life I cannot see through, give me faith and rest, so that I do not lose my reverence for You and my reliance on You. Help me be thankful in ordinary days and choose to trust in the midst of confusion. Because You reign, I am willing to walk forward in peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When You Boldly Ask the Lord, He Will Reach Out and Touch Your Uncleanness
v: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him and he was made clean.
He strictly warned him and immediately sent him out,
and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”

But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places. People came to him from everywhere.
b: This passage in the Gospel records a startling healing miracle: a man with leprosy broke through the boundaries of the law and society and came to Jesus. He did not demand or doubt, but humbly said, “If you want to, you can make me clean.” These words are the height of faith—he firmly believed Jesus had the power, but was not sure whether Jesus was willing.

Jesus’ response was not only words, “I want to,” but action: “he stretched out his hand and touched him.” In that society this was almost unthinkable. Lepers were considered unclean, and touching them meant being isolated oneself. But Jesus did not draw back; he reached out, so that the man was not only healed in body but accepted in heart.

This is a portrait of our own lives—we all have a spiritual “leprosy,” feeling unclean, inadequate, and unaccepted. But when we honestly come before the Lord and say, “Lord, if you want to…” he always answers us, “I want to,” and touches our brokenness and filth with his love, cleansing and restoring us.

Jesus told him to offer the sacrifice according to the law, not to restrict him, but so that he could be accepted again in front of others. Yet the man, in his excitement, disobeyed the Lord’s instruction, and as a result Jesus could no longer enter the city freely. This reminds us that after receiving grace, we must obey and respect the Lord’s heart, responding not only with emotion but with wise action.
a: Boldly bring your uncleanness and pain to Jesus
He is not a God who draws back, but the Lord who reaches out to touch us.
Faith should bring forth obedience, not just emotional enthusiasm
After receiving grace, learn to follow the Lord’s teaching and heart.
Learn from Jesus to reach out and touch the rejected
Having been cleansed, we should also embrace those who are still on the margins.
q: Do I believe the Lord is willing to heal my deepest brokenness? Am I willing, like this man with leprosy, to come boldly before him?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being willing to reach out and touch me at my most unclean and weakest. Help me come to You in faith, and after receiving Your grace, to learn obedience and gratitude and live a life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Jesus Is Alive, and I Have Truly Met Him!
v: That which was from the beginning, that which we have heard, that which we have seen with our eyes, that which we saw, and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life
(and the life was revealed, and we have seen, and testify, and declare to you the life, the eternal life, which was with the Father, and was revealed to us);
that which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have fellowship with us. Yes, and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.
And we write these things to you, that our joy may be fulfilled.
b: John is not discussing a concept but bearing witness to a Lord who is truly alive—Jesus, whom he heard with his own ears, saw with his own eyes, and touched with his own hands. This is not a religious feeling but a fact of life. Jesus is the Word of life from the beginning, the eternal God who became man so that people could draw near and touch him. He is not a lofty idea but a life that truly entered the human world. Jesus is our example; our life begins with him and must be centered on him.

This life did not appear briefly, but was revealed, and is still revealed today to all who believe in him. When we hear the gospel and believe and receive the Lord Jesus, this life enters us, and the Holy Spirit dwells in our hearts, guiding us to live out real change and renewal. It is not by our own struggle, but by being led by the Holy Spirit that we live in his life day by day. The Holy Spirit is our guide, enabling us to experience the presence of the risen Lord, so that faith moves from theory to a real walk together.

And this life is not lonely. The apostle John says he proclaims this life so that we may “have fellowship with us,” and their fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ. When we are connected to the Lord, we also enter a fellowship that belongs to God. This is not merely friendship between people, but a fellowship centered on Jesus, a relationship in which the Lord is King and the Lord rules. In such fellowship our joy can truly be fulfilled, because it is built on love and unity in eternal life.
a: Know the real Lord
Treat Jesus as the real, experienceable Word of life, not as a religious idea.
Obey the Holy Spirit’s guidance
Practice listening to and obeying the Holy Spirit every day, so that life is renewed and transformed.
Live out spiritual fellowship
Take the initiative to connect with other believers and build Lord-centered fellowship and unity.
q: Do I truly treat Jesus as a living Lord, rather than a God in my concepts? Am I willing to step into real fellowship with God and with others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing through Jesus the Word of life that was from the beginning, not an illusory idea but a life we can truly experience. Help me open my heart to hear You, see You, touch You, and have true fellowship with You. Holy Spirit, guide me every day, so that I live out the life of Christ not through my own effort but through You. May I live connected to You and to the body of Christ, so that my joy grows fuller each day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is the true Word of life, and I will walk with him every day!

t: When Jesus Steps In Personally, Your Life Is Never the Same
v: But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
and asked for letters from him to the synagogues of Damascus, that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled, he got close to Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him.
He fell on the earth, and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
He said, “Who are you, Lord?” The Lord said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He said, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.”
The Lord said to him, “Arise and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judah for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus. For behold, he is praying,
and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.”
But the Lord said to him, “Go your way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the children of Israel.
b: Saul was originally the fiercest persecutor of Christians, his heart full of religious zeal and misguided passion. He thought he was zealous for God, not knowing that the one he was truly opposing was Jesus. As he was heading to Damascus to arrest believers, Jesus appeared to him personally. This was not a human arrangement, but a moment when heaven stepped in and salvation came down on its own initiative.

Jesus said to Saul, “Why are you persecuting me?” This shows us that when we hurt the Lord’s disciples, we hurt the Lord himself. Jesus and believers are one; he has a deep union with us. Saul asked, “Who are you, Lord?” This is the question at the turning point of a life. When a person truly meets Jesus and recognizes him as Lord, everything changes.

Saul’s eyes were blind, but his spiritual eyes began to open. He experienced his own helplessness and blindness, and learned to rely on others to lead him. At this time God called another disciple—Ananias. He was an unnamed small figure, yet he played a role that changed history. He did not run away but answered, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.” This is the attitude of a life that lets Jesus be King and lets the Holy Spirit lead.

God’s plan is beyond human imagination. He said Saul was his “chosen vessel” to bear his name before the nations. The persecutor became a preacher; the enemy became an important vessel in God’s hands. This is the power of the gospel and the reversing principle of God’s divine order—old self becomes new self, brokenness becomes a vessel.
a: Stop and turn to the Lord
Do not rely only on your own zeal and direction; let Jesus step into your life personally.
Open your heart to respond to the call
When God calls you, do not delay. Learn from Ananias to say, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.”
Become a vessel in God’s hands
Whatever your past, God can turn you around so that you live for his name.
q: Am I willing to let Jesus change my original road? Am I willing, like Ananias, to become his vessel when God sends me?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You did not wait for me to change before coming to find me, but appeared to me on my mistaken road. Help me set down my pride and stubbornness, turn to You, and hear Your voice. When You call me, give me courage like Ananias to say, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.” I want to be Your chosen vessel and live for Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am willing to obey the call and become a vessel of glory in God’s hands!

t: When You Feel Powerless, You Can Still Strive Together for God’s Work
v: Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,
that I may be delivered from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
that I may come to you in joy through the will of God, and together with you, find rest.
Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
b: In this passage Paul does not present himself as a strong spiritual giant, but humbly asks the brothers and sisters to strive together with him in prayer for him. He knew that even the strongest servant has weakness and risk. His ministry faced persecution, disobedient people, and an uncertain future, yet he chose not to carry it alone, inviting everyone to pray together in one heart through the love of Jesus and the Spirit.

This passage shows an important trait of God’s divine order: united prayer is the strength of working together. Paul says “strive together,” a phrase that carries the sense of “fighting side by side,” showing that prayer is not just gentle religious language but a spiritual battle and walking together. Though not all of us can go to the front lines of mission as Paul did, every believer can stand shoulder to shoulder with God’s servants through prayer and take part in God’s Kingdom plan.

Paul’s prayer requests also carry spiritual wisdom: not just asking for protection, but asking that what he does would please God and be accepted by all, and that he could go forward smoothly according to God’s will. This is the attitude of letting Jesus be King and walking in God’s will. He ends with a blessing: may the God of peace be with you all. This is exactly the unity and rest under the Holy Spirit’s leading—not striving for peace on our own, but letting God’s presence bring peace.
a: Take part in ministry through prayer
Even if I cannot join in person, I can still be a coworker in God’s Kingdom through prayer.
Fight together in one heart
Do not carry everything alone. Learn to humbly ask for prayer and boldly pray for others.
Let God be King and guide
Pray not only for success, but that God’s will be done and his name be glorified.
q: Do I take the power of prayer lightly? Am I willing to strive as an intercessor who stands in the gap? Have I entrusted my plans to God and let him lead?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching me through Paul’s example that prayer is not a sideline but a spiritual battle. Put a love and responsibility for intercession in my heart, so that I am not indifferent or a bystander, but take part in Your work on earth in unity. Help me also to learn to humbly ask for prayer and not carry everything alone. May my life be led by You, go forward in Your will, and rest in Your peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Though I am small, through prayer I can fight alongside God’s work and win the victory!

t: The Hand of God Helps Those Who Set Their Hearts
v: this Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him all his request, according to the LORD his God’s hand on him.
Some of the children of Israel, including some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
He came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
For on the first day of the first month he began to go up from Babylon; and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God on him.
For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.
Now this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, even the scribe of the words of the LORD’s commandments, and of his statutes to Israel:
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the LORD’s house which is in Jerusalem;

and has extended loving kindness to me before the king and his counselors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. I was strengthened according to the LORD my God’s hand on me, and I gathered together chief men out of Israel to go up with me.
b: Ezra’s life did not start from position, power, or background, but from “setting his heart.” He resolved to seek God’s word, study it, obey it, and teach it to others. This resolve made him a vessel God used greatly. God’s hand greatly helped him because of his resolve and faithfulness. Ezra, in the Old Testament, reminds us that those who are willing to obey God’s word are the ones who truly match God’s heart.

He was not merely a scribe with knowledge, but one who made God’s law the standard of his life. He obediently responded to God’s prompting, and not only obeyed himself but taught the truth to the people, restoring the relationship between God’s people and God. This is the model of a God-centered leader in the Old Testament—not acting on his own ideas, but fulfilling God’s plan under God’s guidance.

When Ezra set his heart like this, God’s hand intervened in everything. The king’s heart was moved, the resources and permission to travel were prepared, and every difficulty was removed one by one. This was no accident but a sign that God himself was reigning. When we are willing to go forward according to his heart, he will also strengthen us with his mighty hand and open the way for us.
a: Resolve to obey the Lord’s word
Do not stop at knowing; truly do it.
Live an obedient life
Let God’s word be the standard for how you live.
Rely on the help of God’s hand
Do not rely on yourself, but trust God’s leading and accomplishment.
q: Am I willing to set my heart to truly obey God’s word? Do I believe that when I obey, God’s hand will help me?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Ezra’s example that when I set my heart to obey Your law, Your hand personally helps me. Help me not only understand Your word but have the courage to put it into practice and bring influence through an obedient life. I believe Your hand is still at work, to strengthen me, use me, and lead me into the plan You have prepared. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I resolve to obey God’s word, and his hand will strengthen me to the end!

t: Fearing God and Walking in His Way Is the Path of Blessing
v: The LORD heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me; and the LORD said to me, “I have heard the voice of the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They have well said all that they have spoken.
Oh that there were such a heart in them that they would fear me and keep all my commandments always, that it might be well with them and with their children forever!
You shall observe to do therefore as the LORD your God has commanded you. You shall not turn away to the right hand or to the left.
You shall walk in all the way which the LORD your God has commanded you, that you may live and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which you shall possess.
b: This passage shows us God’s heart: he does not demand legalistic obedience, but longs for his people to fear him from the heart and gladly keep his commandments. He says, “Oh that there were such a heart in them to fear me…” This is God’s sigh, and also his expectation of us—not a brief enthusiasm, but a lasting, steady reverence that comes from the heart.

Reverence is not fear, but honor—the attitude that flows naturally from knowing his greatness and holiness. Such reverence leads us on the right path and makes us willing to follow his guidance. When we do as he commands, without turning to the right or to the left, we make his word the standard of our lives. This is the foundation of God’s divine order and the way of blessing.

God promises that if we do this, not only will we be blessed, but our descendants will be blessed and our days will be long in the land. This is a blessing passed from the inside out and from one generation to the next. And the key to all of it is whether we resolve to fear God and do what he says.
a: Keep a heart of reverence
Remind yourself daily that God is a holy, just, and loving Lord.
Walk according to God’s way
Let God’s word be the basis and direction of your life.
Do not turn to the right or left
Hold to the right path in your choices and do not be led astray by circumstances or feelings.
q: Does my heart truly fear God? Am I living out his word and becoming a blessed person?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for gladly revealing Your heart to me. You do not seek outward obedience, but long for me to have a heart that fears You. Lord, help me in my daily life not to turn to the right or left, but to do according to Your word. Let me and my family be blessed in Your way and live long and secure. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will fear God and walk in his way, and spend my life on the path of blessing!

t: Let God’s Word Hold You Up in Your Low Places and Weakness
v: Then I wouldn’t be disappointed, when I consider all of your commandments.
I will give thanks to you with uprightness of heart, when I learn your righteous judgments.
I will observe your statutes. Don’t utterly forsake me.
How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.
I declared my ways, and you answered me. Teach me your statutes.
Let me understand the teaching of your precepts! Then I will meditate on your wondrous works.
My soul is weary with sorrow; strengthen me according to your word.
Keep me from the way of deceit. Grant me your law graciously!
b: In this passage the psalmist opens his heart completely to God in the midst of trouble and sorrow. He is not pouring out his heart to people, but to God, because he knows that only God’s word can truly hold up the weight on his soul, keep him from shame, and make him stand firm. The psalmist values God’s commandments because he knows these words are the most reliable support in his life.

The psalmist not only cries to God for help, but longs for God’s teaching. He asks God to teach him to understand the precepts so that he can meditate on God’s wondrous works. This is more than reading God’s word; it is entering into the knowledge and praise of what God has done, a turning and training of the heart. He does not run from sorrow, but lets God’s word become a light in it, so that his soul is upheld.

He also admits his weakness, knowing he is prone to stray from the right path, so he asks God to remove him from the way of deceit and grant him his law. This shows a humble heart that longs for change. He understands that true cleansing and uprightness come not from his own effort, but from God’s word coming into his heart and becoming the direction and strength of his life.
ah: Relying on God’s Word in Low Places
a: Make God’s word your source of strength
Read at least one passage of Scripture every day and let God’s word comfort your heart.
Adjust your focus with God’s word
When you are discouraged or upset, think of what God has done before and recover hope.
Humbly ask God for his way
When you are lost or weak, ask God to lead you away from the wrong direction and back to the right path.
q: When I am low and my spirit is dry, am I willing to let God’s word hold me up and guide me, above my own thoughts and feelings?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for never abandoning me. When I am weak and in distress, Your word becomes the support of my soul. Help me learn to meditate on Your truth and no longer live by my own emotions and experience. Graciously teach me and lead me, so that I walk in the way that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God’s word is my strength in the valley and the foundation that makes my heart stand firm!

t: Trust God with Simple Faith, Like a Child
v: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.
But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
b: In this passage Jesus not only welcomes little children, but lifts up their qualities as the model for entering God’s Kingdom. When the disciples, out of grown-up habit, thought the children were unworthy and too insignificant and tried to stop them, Jesus openly expressed his indignation. What he saw was a simple, trusting heart that wanted to be near him, and that is exactly what God delights in.

Jesus said, “The Kingdom of God belongs to such as these.” This does not mean children automatically belong to the Kingdom, but stresses that those who are willing to be like children—simple in trust, not contending for position, relying on God without defenses—are the ones who can truly receive the Kingdom. The threshold of entering the Kingdom is not merit, learning, or ability, but a simple heart.

Jesus not only taught, but embraced the children with his own arms and laid hands on them to bless them. It is an extremely tender scene, showing how much love and compassion God has for those who come to him simply. He will not reject us. If we set down the complexity and self in our hearts and come simply before him, we will be blessed.
ah: Practicing a Heart of Simple Trust
a: Learn to trust simply like a child
Set down your own judgments and self-protection, and simply believe God’s word and promises.
Draw near to Jesus on your own initiative
Like a child running to a parent, come to God every day and draw near to him.
Bring blessing through intercession
Like those who brought children to Jesus, bring others to the Lord too, asking him to touch them personally.
q: Do I still keep a heart of simple trust? Or have doubt, pride, or reasoning blocked my steps toward Jesus?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your gentle embrace and blessing. You do not reject me, but welcome me to come near like a child. Lord, remove all doubt and hardness from my heart, and give me a simple trusting heart again, so that I am blessed in Your presence every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will trust God simply like a child, draw near to him every day, and be blessed by him!

t: Jesus Is My Way Home to the Father
v: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.
In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you.
If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.
You know where I go, and you know the way.”
Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.
If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on, you know him and have seen him.”
b: These are some of the most comforting and tender words Jesus spoke to his disciples on the eve of the cross. He knew their hearts were confused and uneasy, so he spoke words full of promise and hope, urging them, “Don’t let your heart be troubled.” Jesus does not deny that suffering is real; he gives an assured answer: he has prepared an eternal dwelling place for us, and he will surely come again to take us to himself.

He said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” This is not a philosophical claim but an invitation of love. Jesus does not merely point to a road that leads to God; he himself is the road. He is the only bridge that brings us to the Father, and the only door into the Kingdom of God. He is the source of our life, the truth that never changes, and the way to eternity.

Thomas’s question speaks for many on the journey of faith: “How can we know the way?” Jesus’ answer is the answer for all humanity: it comes not through understanding but through relationship, not through what we do but through trusting him. If you follow Jesus closely, you will never lose your direction, and he will personally bring you home to the Father’s house.
ah: Trusting Jesus’ Guidance in Hard Times
a: Overcome temporary sorrow with eternal hope
When you are troubled, remember the eternal home Jesus has prepared for you. Let heavenly hope comfort your heart and rise above present difficulties.
Follow Jesus’ footsteps in faith
When you feel lost, don’t lean on your own plans or reasoning. Return to Jesus’ word and presence; he is the way that never goes wrong.
Practice trust by walking with him daily
Spend time with the Lord each day, reading Scripture and praying. Learn to look to him for guidance in matters big and small, and build the habit of walking with him.
q: Am I focusing on my circumstances and overlooking the way Jesus has already prepared? Do I truly trust him to lead me in the Father’s will?
pr: Dear Lord Jesus, thank you for speaking words of comfort to me when I am troubled and anxious. You are my way, my truth, and my life. I want to follow You closely. Even when the road ahead is unclear, as long as You are with me, my heart has peace. Lead me on the right path until the day I see Your face. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is my way. He brings me home to the Father’s house, and I will trust him all my life and never be lost!

t: Fan Into Flame the Fire Within You
v: For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,
who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News.
For this I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this cause I also suffer these things. Yet I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day.
b: From prison, the apostle Paul wrote these words to encourage his young co-worker Timothy, reminding him not to let his spiritual passion die out, but to fan into flame the gift God had given him. This is not about mere enthusiasm. God has already placed in us a spirit of power, love, and self-control, not a spirit of fear. We need not be afraid of hardship, because God himself has called us and supplies the strength.

In verses 8 to 10, Paul turns to the heart of the gospel: this is grace that is not earned by works, but that God purposed in Christ before time began. The appearing of Jesus not only abolished death, it brought imperishable, eternal life to those who believe in him. This truth is not a theory but a gospel that changes lives, worth suffering for and worth living out as our mission.

Finally, Paul testifies, “I know him whom I have believed.” This is a firm faith, built not on smooth circumstances or reliable people, but on knowing God and being fully persuaded of him. He trusts that the Lord will guard all that he has entrusted to him until the day of the Lord’s return. Such conviction is the source of strength that lets us hold on to our calling and face challenges today.
ah: Let the Fire God Gave You Burn Again
a: Rekindle the passion and gifts God gave you
Don’t let weariness and fear drown your calling. Ask the Lord to help you fan the divine fire into flame again and to use the gifts he has given you once more.
Refuse timidity and be strong in the Lord
When you face challenges or shame, don’t shrink back or run away. Rely on the power, love, and self-control God gives, and bear bold witness to the gospel.
Trust his plan and his keeping
Even in hardship, hold tightly to the Lord you believe in. Trust that he will guard everything you have placed in his hands until he comes again.
q: Do I still remember the stirring and calling God first gave me? Has that fire been smothered? How can I let God fan it into flame again so that I live for him?
pr: Lord, thank you for calling me from the beginning by Your grace. Fan into flame the fire within me again, so that I will not be timid or shrink back, but keep going by the spirit of power, love, and self-control that You give. Even in the face of challenges, I know You reign and will guard me until You come again. May I live out the mission You have given me, to the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have a spirit of power, love, and self-control within me. The Lord will keep me, and I will boldly live for the gospel!

t: Look to God: Victory Is Not in Our Hands
v: Then some came who told Jehoshaphat, saying, “A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea from Syria. Behold, they are in Hazazon Tamar” (that is, En Gedi).
Jehoshaphat was alarmed, and set himself to seek the LORD. He proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
Judah gathered themselves together to seek help from the LORD. They came out of all the cities of Judah to seek the LORD.
and he said, “LORD, the God of our fathers, aren’t you God in heaven? Aren’t you ruler over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in your hand, so that no one is able to withstand you.
Didn’t you, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham your friend forever?
They lived in it, and have built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,

‘If evil comes on us—the sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine—we will stand before this house, and before you (for your name is in this house), and cry to you in our affliction, and you will hear and save.’
Now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned away from them, and didn’t destroy them;
behold, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of your possession, which you have given us to inherit.
Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”

and he said, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat. The LORD says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
b: When a vast enemy army closed in, King Jehoshaphat’s first reaction was fear. But he was not swallowed up by it. Instead, he immediately “set himself to seek Yahweh.” He did not scramble for his own solutions or rush to deploy his troops; he called the whole nation to fast and pray together and seek God’s help. This is how a leader responds who fears God and humbly depends on him.

In his prayer, Jehoshaphat did not begin by asking God to act. He began by declaring God’s sovereignty and faithfulness. He looked back at how God had given Israel the land, and remembered the promise that God would hear his people when they cried out in distress. He did not lean on his army or his experience; he frankly admitted his own helplessness: “We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”

Through the prophet, God encouraged his people: “The battle is not yours, but God’s.” This sentence is the heart of the whole passage. True faith is not the absence of fear; it is choosing to look to God in the midst of fear, handing the control back to God, and knowing that the key to victory lies not in our ability but in what God does.
a: Choose to seek God in the midst of fear
When trouble comes, do I, like Jehoshaphat, seek God and call on him right away, instead of frantically grabbing at human methods?
Hand control to God and don’t rely on yourself
Our eyes should be fixed on God, not frightened by the enemy or our circumstances. It is not we who must win the battle; God will fight for us.
Declare God’s faithfulness in prayer
Often recall in prayer what God has done and hold on to his promises. This makes our faith strong and keeps our hearts from wavering.
q: What pressure or difficulty am I facing right now? Am I willing to admit my helplessness and learn to look to God alone? Do I believe that the victory truly belongs to God?
pr: Dear Lord, I admit that sometimes I am afraid and don’t know what to do. Thank you for letting me know that I can come boldly to seek You and entrust everything to You. Lord, my eyes are on You alone; please fight for me Yourself. Teach me not to rely on myself or my own strength, but to walk by faith and to experience Your deliverance and victory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not rely on myself. My eyes are fixed on God. He will fight for me, and I will not be afraid!

t: Even in the Deepest Pain, Turn to God
v: “Look, LORD; for I am in distress. My heart is troubled. My heart turns over within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Abroad, the sword bereaves. At home, it is like death.

“They have heard that I sigh. There is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble. They are glad that you have done it. You will bring the day that you have proclaimed, and they will be like me.
“Let all their wickedness come before you. Do to them as you have done to me for all my transgressions. For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.
b: This is a cry of terrible pain, the despairing voice of Jerusalem under judgment and destruction. In this passage we see a broken heart pouring out all its anguish before God. It does not hide its own transgressions; instead it confesses before God, “I have grievously rebelled.” This is deep repentance, and it is also a turning of faith.

“Abroad the sword bereaves. At home it is like death.” These words paint a picture of being surrounded on every side with nothing to lean on. And the most heartbreaking line is: “There is no one to comfort me.” The deepest pain in this world is often not outward trouble but the loneliness of being understood by no one and accompanied by no one. Yet even so, the writer still calls out, “See, Yahweh.” That is an act of faith, believing that God is still there and sees everything.

God has never promised that we will not suffer, but he promises that he will not forsake those who turn to him. When we are willing to lift our eyes to God in the midst of pain, this is the beginning of faith. It is not waiting until everything is restored to lean on him, but holding firmly to God’s justice, love, and salvation even in the deepest night.
ah: Learning to Turn in Faith During Suffering
a: Face your brokenness honestly
God is not afraid of our weakness. He wants a heart of true repentance. Don’t suppress your feelings or pretend. Bring all the turmoil and distress of your heart to him.
Turn to God in your loneliness
People may abandon you, misunderstand you, or even gloat over you, but God never leaves. Even when no one comforts us, God sees our sighs and understands our burdens.
Entrust your sense of injustice to the Lord

Jeremiah did not take revenge himself but handed his enemies over to God’s judgment. We too must learn to leave our grievances in the hands of the righteous God, not avenging ourselves, but trusting in God’s judgment and God’s timing.
q: Am I willing to keep believing in God’s love and justice even in pain? Am I willing to pour out honestly to God the distress and the sin in my heart?
pr: Dear Lord, I confess that my sin and rebellion have plunged me into darkness and made me distant from You. My heart is turned over and troubled, and around me there is no comfort and no way out, but I know You still watch over me. Hear my cry, forgive me, and hold me up. Show me grace in my sorrow. Comfort my heart and renew my spirit, so that even in despair I can still look to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Even in pain I still look to God. He is my only hope!

t: Practicing a Life of Inner Peace
v: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!”
Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.
In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report: if there is any virtue and if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
Do the things which you learned, received, heard, and saw in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
b: This passage is like a warm letter to the soul, written to us who struggle under pressure and unease. Paul does not just urge us to “rejoice”; he adds emphasis: “Again I will say, Rejoice!” This is not blind optimism but joy built on faith “in the Lord.” True joy does not come from smooth circumstances but from a relationship connected to the Lord.

When we choose not to worry, but to tell God everything in prayer, we step into a “peace which surpasses all understanding.” This peace does not mean every problem is solved. It is an assurance from God in the heart that keeps us steady in the storm. This is the fruit of faith: inner rest that overcomes outward turmoil.

Finally, Paul reminds us that what we think about shapes the quality of our lives. If we daily think about what is true, just, pure, and lovely, and follow the examples of those who live out their faith, the peace of God will keep being with us.
ah: A Life of Peace Is Practiced
a: Make joy a choice, and don’t be held hostage by emotions
Whatever your circumstances, “rejoice in the Lord always.” This is an attitude of faith, an inner conviction that God is faithful.
Replace anxiety with prayer
Instead of being anxious, pray. Give every need, confusion, and burden to God with thanksgiving, and his peace will guard your heart so the waves do not swallow you.
Deliberately choose good thoughts
Learn to manage your thoughts and cultivate the habit of “thinking about” these things, turning your mind to what is true, honorable, pure, and full of hope.
q: When I feel anxious, do I choose to connect with God through prayer? Am I willing to practice, every day, keeping my thoughts pure and my joy rooted in faith?
pr: Lord, teach me to rejoice in You even in difficulty, and to choose not to worry under pressure. Help me learn to commune with You in prayer and to look to Your provision with a thankful heart. May the peace You give, which surpasses understanding, guard my heart and mind, so that each day I think on Your goodness and do what pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I rejoice in the Lord, I entrust everything to him in prayer, and God’s peace guards my heart every day!

t: Experiencing God’s Provision in the Wilderness
v: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel. Speak to them, saying, ‘At evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
In the evening, quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
When the dew that lay had gone, behold, on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread which the LORD has given you to eat.

This is the thing which the LORD has commanded: ‘Gather of it everyone according to his eating; an omer a head, according to the number of your persons, you shall take it, every man for those who are in his tent.’”
b: In the wilderness, the Israelites faced scarcity and uncertainty, and they began to grumble. Yet God did not punish them for their complaints. He answered their need with grace: quail in the evening, manna in the morning, feeding them day after day until they entered the Promised Land.

This passage is more than a record of a miracle; it is a lesson in faith. When we think the wilderness of life has no way out, God prepares in the morning a provision we have never seen before. He wants us to depend on him every day, taking no more and no less, just enough. This is the Heavenly Father’s daily grace.

Every grain of manna and every quail was God’s intimate care for his people. God does not reveal himself only in great events; he shows that he is our God in our most basic daily needs. When we learn to trust and stop grumbling, we can experience God’s wonderful provision and presence in everyday life.
ah: Practicing Trust in the Wilderness
a: Believe in hard times that God hears
Although the Israelites complained, God still heard their voice. When we are in difficulty, we must not dwell in dissatisfaction, but choose to cry out to God, trusting that he will care for us.
Daily grace is enough for each day

God told the Israelites to gather manna “according to the number of persons,” neither more nor less. This reminds us that God’s provision is not an excess to stockpile, but a faithfulness that is just enough, day after day.
Receive grace, and keep God’s order
God’s provision is not a free-for-all; it comes with commands and boundaries as a discipline. Trusting God is not only waiting for him to act, but also obeying and acting within his instructions.
q: Am I willing to believe that God is already preparing for me when I cannot see a way out? Am I willing to practice faith every day, without grumbling or greed, receiving only according to God’s direction?
pr: Lord, I thank You that in my wilderness days You still look after me with grace. Even when I have complained and my faith has been weak, You have not abandoned me; You have fed me and comforted me Yourself. Lord, teach me to depend on Your faithfulness each day, not to worry about tomorrow, but to be faithful today. Help me not to grumble in difficulty or lose heart in lack, for You are the God who provides for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: In the wilderness, God provides daily. The Lord will not let me lack what I need each day!

t: Renewed Strength, Soaring on Wings
v: Behold, the Lord GOD will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.
He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;
but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
b: This passage portrays two images that seem contradictory yet blend perfectly in God: he is both a ruling King and a gentle Shepherd. He has the power to execute judgment, and he has the love to hold wounded hearts. This almighty and loving God is the one we wait for, the source of our strength.

Each of us experiences weariness and weakness. However young or physically strong we are, there are times we fall. But God’s promise is this: if we wait on him, trust him, and do not rely on ourselves, we will renew our strength and mount up on wings like eagles. This does not come from human willpower or physical stamina, but from strength that comes down from above.

When you feel you cannot go on, remember: real strength is not squeezed out from within, but received from above. In the process of waiting on God, we are not passively waiting; we are actively trusting and quietly looking to him, and finding renewal in his embrace.
ah: Waiting in Weariness, Strengthened in Weakness
a: Knowing you grow weary is the starting point of renewed strength
Even the strongest people get tired. Admitting weakness is not false spirituality; it is the beginning of real faith. For God gives strength to those who admit they have none.
Waiting is not wasted time but a practice of trust

To wait on God means to hand the control to him, choosing to be still and look to him with focus, not hurried or restless. It is in such waiting that our hearts begin to align with God and strength rises again.
God’s arm has both authority and tenderness
God uses his mighty arm to save, and also uses his arm to hold us. He is not a cold God but a gentle Shepherd. You can rest your weight on him. He knows your frailty and gladly gives you strength.
q: When I am weary and powerless, am I still willing to wait on the Lord and trust his promise? Am I willing to lay down my restlessness and learn to be still before God and be renewed?
pr: Lord, You are my strength and my hope. When I feel exhausted, You do not scold me, but hold me in Your loving arms. Lord, teach me to wait, not to prop myself up by my own effort, but to trust Your provision. As I run the race of life, keep me from growing weary; as I walk through hard times, keep me from fainting. I will mount up with wings like an eagle, for You are the God who renews my strength. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I wait for the Lord, and I will renew my strength!

t: Go With His Authority and Presence
v: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
b: The risen Lord appeared to his disciples on a mountain in Galilee. His words were not only a calling but also a promise. Some worshiped him and some still doubted, yet Jesus first declared, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” This is the foundation of his sending us: not our own strength, but his complete authority.

His command is universal: “Go and make disciples of all nations.” The gospel is not limited by geography or ethnicity; it must cross every barrier to the ends of the earth. This mission includes baptizing people and teaching them to obey all that Jesus commanded. It is an ongoing process of discipleship, not a one-time decision.

Finally, he gave us the most precious promise: “I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” This assures us that on the road of mission we will not be alone. His presence is the wellspring of our faith and courage.
a: Be sure of his authority
In ministry and witness, do not rely on your own ability, but believe that Jesus has all authority in heaven and on earth, and that he can accomplish the mission he has entrusted.
Respond to his sending
Wherever you are, carry a heart to “go,” bringing the gospel to those who do not yet know Jesus and helping them grow as disciples.
Depend on his presence
In challenges and difficulties, remember the Lord’s promise: he is with us always, to the end of the age. This is why we do not fear and do not draw back.
q: When I face my mission, do doubt or timidity still hold me back? How can I lean more deeply on the Lord’s authority and presence and boldly “go” to fulfill what he has entrusted to me?
pr: Lord, thank You for entrusting us with the Great Commission and giving us Your authority and presence. Take away our doubt and timidity, and give us hearts that are obedient and brave, so that we may live out our mission in daily life and lead more people to know You and follow You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I go forth by the Lord’s authority to fulfill my mission, and he is with me to the end of the age!

t: An Attitude of Overcoming Evil With Good
v: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don’t curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Don’t be wise in your own conceits.
Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
Don’t seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to God’s wrath. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.”
Therefore “If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, you will heap coals of fire on his head.”
Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
b: In this passage Paul teaches believers the spiritual attitude to take toward conflict and challenge in relationships. When we are persecuted or hurt, our natural reaction is to strike back or take revenge, but God’s heart is for us to bless the other person, because blessing ends the cycle of hatred and reveals the Heavenly Father’s love.

He also reminds us to enter into other people’s feelings: rejoicing when they rejoice and weeping with them when they weep, which is a concrete expression of love and empathy. Being of the same mind, without pride, willing to associate with the lowly, is how true unity is built.

In the face of evil, we do not repay evil for evil, but take thought for what is honorable in the sight of all, and do our best to live at peace with everyone, not avenging ourselves, since the authority to judge belongs to the Lord. Even toward an enemy we are to meet his needs in love, as if heaping coals of fire on his head, so that his conscience is enlightened and he turns to repentance. In the end, the believer’s victory does not come from overpowering by force, but from overcoming evil with good.
a: Choose blessing instead of revenge
When hurt, do not repay evil with evil. In faith choose to bless, and let love stop hatred.
Live with a humble, empathetic heart
Be willing to enter into others’ joys and sorrows and to associate with the lowly, building genuine unity.
Rely on God to overcome evil with good
Do not avenge yourself. Entrust justice to God, and use goodness to turn hearts and situations around.
q: When I face hurt or injustice, do I choose to hit back, or to bless? How can I more concretely use love to overcome evil?
pr: Dear Lord, You teach me not to be overcome by evil, but to overcome evil with good. Give me a humble, gentle, and forgiving heart, so that I can bless those who persecute me, accompany those in need around me, and still rely on Your judgment in the midst of injustice. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will overcome evil with good and conquer hatred with love!

t: Receiving the Kingdom of God Like a Child
v: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.
But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
b: In this passage Jesus not only welcomes little children, he holds them up as a spiritual example. Children are simple, sincere, and quick to believe. They do not strive for things by their own ability but gladly receive gifts from others. Jesus uses these qualities to illustrate the attitude needed to receive the Kingdom of God: not earning points by deeds, nor relying on status or qualifications, but receiving God’s grace with a heart of simple trust and complete dependence.

In the culture of that day, children were regarded as the lowest in status, with no voice, yet Jesus embraced them and blessed them, overturning the world’s mindset. He wants us to learn a child’s humility and trust, for the Kingdom of God belongs to those who do not rely on themselves but depend completely on God.
ah: Returning to a Child’s Simplicity
a: Trust God with your whole heart
As a child trusts a parent, hand the lordship of your life to God and do not doubt his love and guidance.
Receive grace humbly
Admit that you cannot trade your own ability for salvation; simply receive God’s grace and blessing.
Live out sincere love
In dealing with others, keep a pure and honest heart, refuse scheming and calculation, and bless others with sincerity.
q: Does my faith still keep a simple trust in God, or has it been replaced by life’s calculations and the pressure of reality? Am I willing to return to a child’s faith?
pr: Dear Lord, remove the complicated pride and calculation from my heart and restore a simple heart that loves You and trusts You. Help me not to strive by myself but to rest in Your grace and simply receive Your blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I trust simply like a child, and I will inherit the Kingdom of God!

t: Humbled Before the Almighty
v: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
“I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
Who can strip off his outer garment? Who will come within his jaws?
Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
b: This passage is one of the questions God put to Job. He uses the crocodile (or Leviathan, a huge sea creature) to reveal his power and human limitation. This is not a mere description of an animal; it is a soul-shaking lesson: a creature that looks so fierce and impossible to subdue in human eyes is, to God, only a creature in his hand.

Through the image of this creature, God lets us see how small we are and how high he is. No human skill, wisdom, or strength can subdue it, much less make a covenant with it, yet God is the Lord who creates, rules over, and sustains all things. When we realize that even the most fearsome force in nature is under God’s authority, we understand that before the Almighty the only thing we can do is to be humble, to revere him, and to trust him completely.
a: Admit your limitations
When you face challenges beyond your ability, do not rely on yourself but turn to the almighty God.
Revere God’s authority
Remember that everything belongs to God, and even what humans cannot control is in his hands.
Trust the Lord with all your heart
When trouble looms like a monster, do not panic, but rest in faith in God’s protection and rule.
q: Do I admit that I cannot control everything, and entrust my life completely to God? When I meet difficulties beyond my ability, do I turn to him first?
pr: Almighty Lord, You created and rule over all things, and even what I fear is under Your authority. Give me a heart of humility and reverence, to admit my limits and to trust completely in Your protection and guidance. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I revere the almighty Lord, who reigns over all things!

t: Confess and Forsake, Then Find True Freedom
v: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
b: This passage reveals two completely different paths in life. The first is concealing sin and refusing to admit mistakes. It seems to save face, but spiritually it leads to being shut in and dried up. The second is confessing and forsaking sin, facing God and others humbly, and instead receiving mercy and forgiveness, with the soul set free.

A heart that fears God is a spiritual protection, making us sensitive to whether our steps have strayed from the right path. A soft heart repents immediately under the Holy Spirit’s light, but a hard heart defends itself and resists the truth, and in the end falls into deeper trouble. To be truly blessed is to live in an attitude of reverence for God and to keep returning to his way.
ah: Walking the Path of Mercy
a: Be courageous to admit mistakes
When the Holy Spirit shines his light, confess at once, without making excuses or shifting blame.
Forsake sin completely
Repentance is not only confessing but turning, staying far from the things that make us stumble.
Keep a soft heart
Always keep reverence, let God’s word enter your heart, and don’t let pride or stubbornness cost you your alertness.
q: Have I ever covered up sin because of pride or fear of the consequences? Today, am I willing to open myself fully before God and sincerely forsake whatever separates me from him?
pr: Lord, give me a soft and humble heart, so that I do not cover up or hide, but am willing to confess and completely forsake sin. Help me always to keep reverence and walk in Your path of light, receiving Your mercy and protection. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I confess and forsake sin and always fear God, and I will obtain mercy!

t: Let God’s Word Revive My Heart
v: The LORD’s law is perfect, restoring the soul. The LORD’s covenant is sure, making wise the simple.
The LORD’s precepts are right, rejoicing the heart. The LORD’s commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes.
The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever. The LORD’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether.
They are more to be desired than gold, yes, than much fine gold, sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb.
Moreover your servant is warned by them. In keeping them there is great reward.
Who can discern his errors? Forgive me from hidden errors.
Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins. Let them not have dominion over me. Then I will be upright. I will be blameless and innocent of great transgression.
Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, LORD, my rock, and my redeemer.
b: The psalmist uses a series of descriptions to show how precious and powerful God’s word is: it revives a sleeping soul, gives wisdom to the simple, brings real joy, opens spiritual eyes, and lets us see the light of truth even in darkness. This is not just an ancient book; it is the word of life in which God speaks directly to our hearts.

For the psalmist, God’s word is more precious than gold and sweeter than honey, because it guides the way, protects life, and brings an eternal reward. When we read God’s word, it is not just the accumulation of knowledge but the transformation of the heart. It exposes the hidden sins we cannot see, and keeps us from falling into the snare of presumptuous sin.

Finally, the psalmist offers a beautiful prayer that his words and thoughts would be acceptable before God. This is the ultimate effect of God’s word: to make both our inner heart and our outward conduct pleasing to him.
ah: Love and Live Out God’s Word
a: Let God’s word revive your soul every day
Don’t read Scripture only in hard times; be nourished by the truth every day.
Let God’s word examine and cleanse your heart
Ask the Holy Spirit to shine on our hidden sins so that we are not ruled by sin.
Live a life that pleases God
Not only hear the word but do it, so that our words and thoughts all line up with God’s heart.
q: Do I sincerely cherish God’s word more than wealth and sweet pleasures? Am I willing to let God’s word shine on and change my life every day?
pr: Lord, Your word is my life and my light. Revive my heart day by day, and make me long for Your truth more than any treasure in the world. Shine Your light on me, forgive my hidden sins, and keep me from presumptuous sin, so that my words and thoughts may be acceptable to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Rejoicing in Hope Through Grace
v: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
through whom we also have our access by faith into this grace in which we stand. We rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance;
and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope;
and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
For while we were yet weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
For one will hardly die for a righteous man. Yet perhaps for a good person someone would even dare to die.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we will be saved from God’s wrath through him.
For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life.
Not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
b: This passage lays out the whole picture of Christ’s salvation before us: from justification to reconciliation, from grace to glory, from suffering to hope, from death to life. All of it is grace accomplished through Jesus Christ.

Paul tells us that faith not only reconciles us to God but also lets us stand in grace at every moment of life. Even in suffering we can rejoice, because suffering is not the end but a way of shaping our lives, producing perseverance, proven character, and a hope that never disappoints. This hope does not fail because the Holy Spirit has poured God’s love into our hearts, so that we know deeply that we are loved children.

The most astonishing thing is that Christ did not wait for us to become good before he died for us. While we were still sinners, even enemies of God, he gave his life for our redemption. Now that we are justified by his blood, we can be all the more sure that he will keep us to the end, so that we no longer fear God’s wrath but rejoice in God, living in close relationship with him.
ah: Living Out Joyful Hope in Grace
a: Remember the grace of salvation often
Every day think about being someone justified by faith and reconciled to God, and let gratitude fill your heart.
Hold on to hope in suffering
Don’t let hardship rob your joy, for God is using suffering to shape our lives.
Rejoice in God himself
Be thankful not only for being saved, but rejoice in God for who he is, and enjoy the intimate relationship of walking with him.
q: When circumstances are hard, can I still rejoice in my identity as one reconciled to God? Do I truly rejoice in God above every comfort in this world?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving Your life for me while I was still a sinner, so that I am justified by faith and reconciled to the Father. Help me to stand in grace, rejoicing in hope in every circumstance, and not be defeated by suffering. May I take joy in You all my life and live in the presence of Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I stand in grace, rejoicing in hope, for Christ has reconciled me to God and will keep me to the end!

t: Seeing Jesus Is Seeing the Father
v: Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”
Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you such a long time, and do you not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? The words that I tell you, I speak not from myself; but the Father who lives in me does his works.
Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me; or else believe me for the very works’ sake.
Most certainly I tell you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and he will do greater works than these, because I am going to my Father.
Whatever you will ask in my name, I will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you will ask anything in my name, I will do it.
b: Philip’s request was simple: “Show us the Father.” Yet Jesus’ answer carries a very deep truth: to see him is to see the Father. Jesus’ words and actions, his compassion and power, his truth and justice, fully display the Father’s heart.

Jesus did not merely teach about the Father; he is the revelation of the Father himself. Every word he spoke was the result of the Father working in him. This also reminds us that faith is built not only on what we hear taught but can be strengthened by what he has done. Even if doubts remain, we can come to know him from what he has already accomplished.

Amazingly, Jesus promises that whoever believes in him will not only do the works he did but even greater works, because he is going to the Father. When our prayers are in his name, they are joined to his will and will be answered, so that the Father is glorified in the Son. This is an invitation to enter a life united with the Father and the Son, and to continue his work in love and power.
ah: Living in the Truth of Oneness With the Father
a: Know the Father through Jesus
Meditate on what Jesus said and did in the Gospels, and let him be the mirror through which you know the Heavenly Father.
Answer doubt with faith
Even if you don’t understand everything, remember what he has done in your life and in the lives of others, and let these testimonies strengthen your faith.
Pray in his name
Learn to align your prayers with the heart of Jesus, so that what you ask glorifies the Father.
q: Do I truly believe that seeing Jesus is seeing the Father? Is the ultimate aim of my prayers often to glorify the Father?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for showing me the Father’s heart so that I no longer grope in the dark. Help me each day to know the Heavenly Father more through Your word and works, so that my faith is not shaken. Teach me to pray in Your name, not for my own glory, but to fulfill the Father’s will and bring glory to Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I see Jesus, and so I see the Father. I pray in his name, and the Father will do it, that he may be glorified!

t: Serving Without Counting Life Dear
v: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,
serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;
how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,
testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.
Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;
except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
b: These parting words of Paul are like a spiritual last testament, revealing the resolve of a faithful servant. His service was not built on applause or a safe environment but on commitment to the Lord. He served humbly before all, taught with tears, and held back nothing that would benefit them, whether at the lectern of the synagogue or at the dinner table in a home, faithfully urging people to repent and trust Jesus.

Paul knew that chains and afflictions awaited him, yet he went to Jerusalem “bound by the Spirit,” because his life was already in the Lord’s hands. His focus was not on his own safety but on completing the mission entrusted to him: to testify to the gospel of God’s grace. Such a life shows us what it truly means not to count life dear, and the worth of living for the Lord’s calling to the very last moment.
ah: Learning Paul’s Attitude in Service
a: Faithfully proclaim the truth
Whoever the audience and whatever the setting, do not shrink from sharing God’s word.
Stay focused on the mission and don’t be scared off by hardship
Even when the road ahead is hard, make completing the Lord’s charge your goal.
Place your life in the Lord’s hands
Put your own safety second, and treasure glorifying the Lord and completing your mission above all.
q: When I face an unknown challenge, do I first think of my own safety and interests, or of fulfilling God’s mission?
pr: Lord, give me a heart that is faithful to the end, so that in good times and bad I am willing to proclaim Your truth and carry out what You have entrusted to me. Help me place my life in Your hands, not to be frightened off by difficulty or risk, until I finish the race You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not count my life dear; I only want to complete the mission the Lord has entrusted to me and testify to the gospel of God’s grace!

t: Blessed Through Obeying God’s Word in Trust
v: Now Elisha had spoken to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Arise, and go, you and your household, and stay for a while wherever you can; for the LORD has called for a famine. It will also come on the land for seven years.”
The woman arose, and did according to the man of God’s word. She went with her household, and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
