At the end of seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines. Then she went out to beg the king for her house and for her land.
Now the king was talking with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please tell me all the great things that Elisha has done.”

As he was telling the king how he had restored to life him who was dead, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life begged the king for her house and for her land. Gehazi said, “My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.”

When the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed to her a certain officer, saying, “Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.”
b: This Shunammite woman had earlier received Elisha in faith, and later, in obedience to the prophet’s instruction, moved away with her whole household before the famine. She did not know what the future held, but she chose to believe the word of the man of God. Seven years later she returned home and faced the problem of her property being taken over, but God had already prepared a wonderful arrangement: at the very moment she appealed to the king, the king was hearing the testimony about her. As a result she not only recovered her property but also the harvest of all seven years.

This story reminds us that when we trust and obey God’s word, even if we seem to lose something for a time, God will fully restore it in his time, even more than we expected. God’s preparation is often more detailed and more perfect than we imagine.
ah: Faithful Obedience Brings Restoration
a: Prepare your heart in good times
Like the woman who obeyed God’s word before the famine, learn to listen and trust even in times of peace.
Don’t lose heart in the face of loss
Even if something is taken away for a time, believe that God has the power and the timing to restore.
Testify to what God has done
Boldly share God’s grace in your life; this may become the opening for God to step in.
q: When I face difficulty or loss, am I willing to obey God’s leading first, believing that he has the best arrangement?
pr: Lord, thank You for Your faithfulness and love. Give me faith like the Shunammite woman’s, willing to obey Your word in the unknown and to believe that Your restoration exceeds my imagination. Whatever lies before me, may I always testify to Your grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I obey God’s word, and in his time he will restore me and complete it for me many times over!

t: Strength and Salvation From the Lord
v: Out of my distress, I called on the LORD. The LORD answered me with freedom.
The LORD is on my side. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
The LORD is on my side among those who help me. Therefore I will look in triumph at those who hate me.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD, than to put confidence in man.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD, than to put confidence in princes.
All the nations surrounded me, but in the LORD’s name I cut them off.
They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me. In the LORD’s name I indeed cut them off.
They surrounded me like bees. They are quenched like the burning thorns. In the LORD’s name I cut them off.
You pushed me back hard, to make me fall, but the LORD helped me.
The LORD is my strength and song. He has become my salvation.
b: The psalmist looks back on his experience in distress and testifies how real and powerful the Lord’s help is. The enemy’s attacks swarmed like bees and blazed like fire, but he triumphed in the name of the Lord. This victory was not by his own ability; it came because he took refuge in the Most High, the Almighty.

When people look for something to lean on, we often turn first to people, resources, and power. But the psalmist reminds us: it is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man, for human help is limited, and only God’s salvation can completely turn a situation around and place us in a “spacious place,” a place of peace, freedom, and glory.
ah: Holding On to Dependence on God in Hard Times
a: Make prayer your first reaction in distress
Learn in a crisis to call on God first, rather than panicking or running to others.
Face challenges in the name of the Lord
When fear and pressure surround you, strengthen your heart by declaring, “In the name of Yahweh.”
Give the glory to God
After experiencing deliverance, don’t forget to acknowledge that he is my strength, my song, and my salvation.
q: When I face difficulty, do I first look for human help, or do I take refuge in the Lord alone?
pr: Lord, thank You for hearing my cry in distress and rescuing me from trouble. Help me, whatever I encounter, to rely on Your name, not to be held captive by fear, and always to respond to Your grace with thanksgiving and praise. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord I am strong and courageous. He is my strength, my song, and my salvation!

t: The Decisive Choice in the Face of Temptation
v: The LORD God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed.

Out of the ground the LORD God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’”
The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,
for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.
b: God placed Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden, prepared abundant resources and a beautiful environment, and also drew a clear line: do not eat the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. But Satan cleverly twisted God’s word, first creating doubt, then stirring up desire, and finally leading them to believe that disobeying God was a shortcut to a “better life.” Caught between sensory attraction and a false mindset, Eve made a decisive and fatal choice.

Temptation is often not naked evil at the beginning; it comes dressed as “good to look at, good to eat, and seemingly beneficial.” The devil knows how to start by making us doubt God’s word and then lead us step by step down the path of self-centeredness and rebellion against God. True protection is to remember God’s truth before temptation comes, and to choose to trust his heart over our own feelings.
ah: Building Life Habits That Resist Temptation
a: Know and hold fast to God’s word
Let truth become the standard in your heart, so that when lies appear you can recognize them at once.
Guard your thoughts
Don’t let the lust of the eyes, the lust of the flesh, and the pride of life take root in your heart.
Decide to obey before the temptation comes
Cultivate a settled resolve so that when temptation comes you can refuse it immediately.
q: In my life, which areas are easily drawn by feelings or advantage so that I overlook God’s commands?
pr: Lord, thank You for giving Your word to guide me so that I am not deceived at the crossroads of choice. Give me a clear mind and a firm will, so that in the face of temptation I still choose to obey Your will, for I know that only Your way is true life and freedom. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I resist temptation by God’s word and choose to obey him, and I receive life and blessing!

t: Be Strong and Courageous, Walking With God
v: Now after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ servant, saying,
“Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go across this Jordan, you and all these people, to the land which I am giving to them, even to the children of Israel.
I have given you every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, as I told Moses.
No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.
“Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go.

This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
b: When Moses had completed his mission, the heavy task of taking over fell on Joshua. Facing unknown wars and huge pressure, God charged him three times to “be strong and courageous,” because true courage is rooted not in circumstances or self-confidence but in God’s presence that never leaves or forsakes. God not only promised to be with Joshua but also pointed out the key to success: keep his word, meditate on it day and night, and obey it wholeheartedly.

God’s plans often come with challenges, but his presence and promises are greater than any difficulty. Being strong is not gritting your teeth, and being courageous is not showing off. It is choosing to trust God’s word and follow his guidance, believing that he will open the way even when ahead lie the Jordan River and fortified cities.
ah: Living Out Strong and Courageous Faith
a: Take God’s word as your guide
Let Scripture fill your mouth and heart every day, and become the basis of your actions.
Choose trust over fear
When difficulties come, don’t look at the circumstances first, but fix your eyes on God’s promises.
Experience God’s presence in action
Take steps of faith in the midst of challenges, and you will witness his faithfulness.
q: In the challenges I face, am I looking more to God’s presence and promises, rather than being scared by the difficulties?
pr: Lord, thank You that Your presence is the foundation of my strength. Give me a strong and courageous heart, so that I do not shrink back in challenges or get lost in the unknown. May Your word be my daily guide, so that I prosper and succeed in Your way. All glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Wherever I go, the Lord is with me. I will be strong and courageous, and all will go well!

t: The Way Home: The Father’s Embrace
v: He said, “A certain man had two sons.
The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.
Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
“He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
“But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.
b: The younger son left his father because he thought freedom meant escaping restraint and living as he pleased. But in sin and reckless living he lost far more than money. He lost his dignity, his direction, and his hope. When he “came to himself,” he finally saw that his father’s house was the place of true safety and abundance. The father did not scold him for the past, and he did not first ask whether the son’s repentance was sincere enough. He ran to meet him, embraced him, kissed him, and restored his standing and honor. This is the heart of our heavenly Father: no matter how far we have gone, when we turn back, he gladly receives us completely.
ah: Returning to the Father’s Love
a: Genuine Repentance
Admit your wrongs and turn to God, instead of running away or defending yourself.
Believe You Are Accepted
However badly you have failed, trust that the Father’s love is greater than your sin.
Live Your New Identity
Since you are forgiven, live in the restored honor and calling you have been given, and do not go back to the old life.
q: In my life, where am I still far from the Father’s heart like the younger son? Am I willing today to return to his embrace?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for Your love that never gives up. Help me leave the far country of sin and come quickly back to Your home. May I repent from my heart, receive Your forgiveness and restoration, and live out the honor and calling of Your child every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have come home to the Father. His love accepts me completely. In his embrace I will find new strength and live a new life!

t: Believe, and You Will See the Glory of God
v: Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”
Jesus said to her, “Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?”
So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, “Father, I thank you that you listened to me.
I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”
When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.”
b: When Jesus gave his command, Martha thought of the practical difficulty: “There is a stench.” But Jesus saw the glory the Father was about to reveal. Faith does not deny reality. It chooses to believe that God’s word is more real than our circumstances and carries more authority than our experience. Jesus first thanked the Father for hearing him. This is the prayer of faith: not waiting for the result before giving thanks, but giving thanks ahead of time because God is faithful. When he cried, “Lazarus, come out!” the dead man really did walk out of the tomb, because the words of Jesus carry life and authority. Today he can still call our lives out of death, bondage, and disappointment into freedom.
ah: Roll Away the Stone in Your Heart
a: Put Down the Barriers of Unbelief
Admit the reasons in your heart that make it hard to believe, and ask the Lord to help you roll them away.
Give Thanks First, Then Wait
Learn from Jesus to thank God for what he is doing, even before you see it accomplished.
Answer the Lord’s Call
When the Lord calls you out of some bondage, obey right away and take a step of faith.
q: In my life, which “tomb” does the Lord need to call me out of? Am I willing to believe, so that I may see his glory?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You that You are the Lord of life. Your word can raise the dead and turn despair into hope. Please roll away the unbelief in my heart so that I may see Your glory. May I not be frightened by my circumstances, and when I hear Your call, may I rise and come out into the freedom and abundance You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I believe! I will see the glory of God. He has called me out, into the light of his life and freedom!

t: By Grace, Through Faith
v: You were made alive when you were dead in transgressions and sins,
in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the children of disobedience.
We also all once lived among them in the lusts of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest.
But God, being rich in mercy, for his great love with which he loved us,
even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
and raised us up with him, and made us to sit with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
that in the ages to come he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus;
for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God,
not of works, that no one would boast.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.
b: Paul gives us a sharp contrast. Once we were dead in sin, powerless to save ourselves, following the world and the flesh, and led by evil spirits toward destruction. Now, because of God’s rich mercy and great love, we have been awakened by Christ and made alive. We have been raised with him and seated with him in the heavenly places.

None of this comes from our own effort. It is by grace alone, received through faith. Grace is not a reward for what we do. It is a gift God gives on his own initiative. Faith is not our achievement. It is the act of reaching out empty hands to receive that grace.
Having been born again, we do not go on living as we please. We are to walk in the good path God prepared long ago and become witnesses to his glory.
ah: Live in Grace, Walk in Good Works
a: Always Remember That Grace Saved You
Whatever spiritual fruit you see, do not boast. Simply give thanks.
Respond to Grace with Faith
Read the Bible and pray each day, not to earn grace, but because you have received it and want to draw near to God.
Walk in the Good Works He Prepared
Watch for the opportunities God places before you, and go and love and serve others.
q: Do I still try to “add” my own good deeds to my salvation? Or am I willing to rely on God’s grace alone and do good out of a thankful heart?
pr: Abba Father, thank You that when I was without hope and dead in sin, You redeemed me with Your great love and made me alive together with Christ. Please keep my heart from trusting in my own strength. Help me depend on Your grace and the power of the Holy Spirit every day, walking in the good path You have prepared, so that my whole life brings glory to Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I live by grace, through faith!

t: Meeting the Great Light in the Darkness
v: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. The light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death.
You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder.
For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the day of Midian.
For all the armor of the armed man in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for the fire.
For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this.
b: Isaiah’s prophecy reveals that a people living in darkness and oppression will see a great light. This is no passing glimmer of dawn. It is salvation that God himself has prepared for humankind. The birth of that child is the turning point where God’s plan enters history.

His coming brings not only joy but also release. The yoke and rod that crushed people will be broken, and the scars and traces of war will no longer rule human destiny. For this child is more than a child. He is “Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace,” and his reign brings justice, peace, and lasting security.

Looking back today, we can clearly see this prophecy fulfilled in Christ. Jesus came into the world to light a hope in the darkness, to give us joy in despair, and to bring true freedom in the midst of sin and fear.
a: Look to the Light in the Darkness
When life falls into difficulty, choose to fix your eyes on Christ, the light that never goes out in the darkness.
Give Thanks in Joy
Remember that God has already broken the sin and fear that held us, and be thankful and glad often.
Follow in Peace
Take Christ as your Prince of Peace, and learn to treat others with justice, righteousness, and love.
q: Am I willing to let Jesus be the “Prince of Peace” in my life? Which dark corners of my life need his light to shine in?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for sending Your only Son into the world to be my light and my hope. When I am in darkness and difficulty, let Your light shine on me and give me joy and release. Help me follow You in my daily life and treat others with justice, righteousness, and love, showing the Kingdom of Your peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is the great light in my darkness, and the Prince of Peace over my life!

t: Choosing the Feast of Wisdom
v: Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.
She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her wine. She has also set her table.
She has sent out her maidens. She cries from the highest places of the city:
“Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,
“Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!
Leave your simple ways, and live. Walk in the way of understanding.”
One who corrects a mocker invites insult. One who reproves a wicked man invites abuse.
Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
b: Wisdom is pictured here as a diligent hostess who carefully builds her house, prepares a feast, and eagerly invites people to share it. She calls out especially to the simple and the foolish, because God’s wisdom is not reserved for those who think themselves clever. It is prepared for those who are willing to admit they need help. This is an invitation of grace. Enter the feast of wisdom and you can leave foolishness behind, receive true life, and walk in the way of light.

But the passage also reminds us that our attitude decides whether we can receive wisdom. The scoffer, out of pride, refuses instruction and may even attack the one who corrects him. The wise person humbly receives correction and grows all the more because of it. So entering the feast of wisdom does not depend on outward status or cleverness. It depends on a humble, teachable heart.
a: Respond to Wisdom’s Invitation
Spend time in God’s word each day. It is like sitting at wisdom’s table and receiving the bread of life.
Leave the Path of Foolishness
Actively let go of habits and choices that do not please God, and learn to walk in the light.
Keep a Humble, Teachable Heart
When you are reminded or corrected, do not rush to defend yourself. Reflect, receive it, and let it make you wiser.
q: Is there still foolish choice or habit in my life? Am I willing to be humble, answer God’s invitation, and sit at his table of wisdom every day?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for preparing the feast of wisdom and inviting me to receive life. Help me throw away foolishness and choose to walk in the way of light. Give me a humble, teachable heart that grows from Your word and from the reminders of others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I choose to enter the feast of wisdom, leave foolishness behind, and walk in the way of light!

t: Living for the Lord as a New Creation
v: Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.
For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ that each one may receive the things in the body according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God, and I hope that we are revealed also in your consciences.
For we are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer those who boast in appearance and not in heart.
For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if we are of sober mind, it is for you.
For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.
He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.
Therefore we know no one according to the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.
Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
b: This passage reminds us that the most important aim in life is not to build ourselves up but “to be well pleasing to him.” One day we will all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ and receive according to what we have done. That means our lives are not to be squandered, but lived before God with reverence.

Paul stresses that his motivation is not fame or appearance but “the love of Christ compels us.” Because Jesus died and rose again for us, we have new life, and the purpose of this life is to “no longer live to ourselves, but to him who died and rose again for our sakes.” In Christ we are a new creation. The old has passed away, and all things have become new.

God has not only changed our identity. He has also entrusted us with a mission: to be his ambassadors, carrying the ministry of reconciliation. This is not an optional task. It is a glorious trust from God, to pass on the message of reconciliation so that more people receive new life through the love of Christ.
a: Make It Your Aim to Please the Lord
In whatever circumstances you live, make being well pleasing to him the highest goal of your life.
Live Out Your New Creation Identity
Put down old bondage and sin, and live in the renewed pattern of life you have in Christ.
Be an Ambassador of Reconciliation
Seize opportunities to share Christ’s love and the gospel, and invite people to be reconciled to God.
q: Am I living for myself right now, or for the Lord who died and rose for me? Am I really walking in my identity as a new creation?
pr: Dear Lord, thank You that Your love compels me, so that I no longer live for myself but for You. Help me each day to make it my aim to please You, to live out my new life, and to be Your ambassador, bringing the gospel of reconciliation to more people. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am a new creation in Christ. The old has passed away, and I will live for the Lord!

t: Obeying God’s Leading in Danger
v: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”
He arose and took the young child and his mother by night and departed into Egypt,
and was there until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
b: This passage looks like a simple story of fleeing as refugees, yet it is full of God’s sovereignty and protection. Herod’s scheme was cruel and murderous, but God had already prepared a way out. Through an angel in a dream, he gave Joseph clear direction and kept the infant Jesus from harm. This reminds us that even when the world is full of darkness and persecution, God’s hand still rules history, and his plan will never fail.

Joseph’s obedience is also precious. He did not delay or argue. He “arose by night” and took Mary and the child to Egypt right away. This was an act of faith. Though the road looked strange and dangerous, he trusted God’s word and was willing to follow without hesitation. Because of that, the life of Jesus was preserved and God’s plan of salvation moved forward.

Here the prophet’s word is fulfilled, showing God’s heart from ancient times to now. He governs all things, and even through persecution and hardship he still accomplishes his plan of redemption. Today we too can be sure that whatever our circumstances, God will watch over his children and guide us in his will.
a: Trust God’s Protection
Even in danger and challenge, believe that God’s plan is higher than human schemes.
Obey and Act Immediately
When God prompts you through his word or the Holy Spirit, do not delay or hesitate. Respond at once.
Be Sure of God’s Promises
God’s word will not fail. What he has spoken over your life will surely come to pass.
q: When God moves me to do something, do I delay, question, or obey right away?
pr: Dear Father, thank You that You reign even in darkness and danger. Give me faith and courage to obey Your leading at once, as Joseph did. Help me believe in Your protection and promises, so that I walk in Your will at every step. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I choose to obey God’s leading right away, for he will keep me and fulfill his plan!

t: A Body That Cares for One Another
v: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,
while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,
that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
b: Using the picture of a body, Paul reminds us that the church is not made of independent individuals but of members joined together and dependent on one another. No one can say, “I don’t need you,” because every person has been placed by God’s own hand. Members who seem weak or unremarkable to people are indispensable in God’s eyes, and they need even more care and respect.

This design keeps us from division and holds the whole body together. When one member suffers, the whole body feels the pain. When one member is honored, everyone rejoices together. This is how the church should be: caring for one another, building one another up, and working together in unity to live out the body of Christ.
a: Acknowledge One Another’s Importance
Whatever our position or the size of our gifts, every brother and sister is valued by God.
Care Especially for the Weak
Learn to reach out to members who are overlooked or struggling, and give them extra care and help.
Share Sorrows and Joys
Do not carry your pain alone, and do not hold back your joy. Let the group carry burdens and celebrate together.
q: Have I looked down on some members, or felt that I am dispensable? How will I live out caring for one another in my community today?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for making me a part of the body of Christ. Help me recognize the value of every member, love especially the weak, and learn to share both suffering and joy. May Your church be united and bring glory to Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am indispensable in the body of Christ, and we will care for one another and glorify the Lord together in unity!

t: Having the Mind of Christ
v: If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.
Therefore God also highly exalted him, and gave to him the name which is above every name,
that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
b: This passage lays the foundation for Christian unity and humility. Paul says that if we truly have encouragement in Christ, the comfort of love, and fellowship in the Spirit, then we should be of one mind and one love in our thinking, and so give a united witness.

He reminds us that unity is not built on power or self-exaltation but on humility: counting others better than ourselves, and looking not only to our own needs but also to the good of others. This attitude is exactly what it means to follow the heart of Christ.

Jesus, who was in the form of God, chose to empty himself, take the form of a servant, and become obedient even to death on a cross. Because of this, God highly exalted him and gave him the name above every name. One day every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. This is the glory that humility and obedience bring.
a: Pursue Unity
Do not quarrel out of factions or vanity. Work to be one with your brothers and sisters in thought and love.
Learn Humble Service
Count others more significant than yourself, and take the initiative to care for their needs.
Follow Christ’s Example
Let Christ’s humility and obedience shape your own attitude toward life, so that his mind becomes your mind.
q: In daily life, do I focus more on my own needs and overlook the good of others? How will I practically have the mind of Christ today?
pr: Lord, thank You for humbling Yourself and bearing the cross for me, to complete my salvation. Give me a humble and obedient heart so that I can care for others, be united with my brothers and sisters, and live in the likeness of Christ. May my life glorify Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will have the mind of Christ, humble and obedient, for the glory of God!

t: Peace in Christ
v: Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?
Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
b: Before his suffering, Jesus spoke these words to his disciples. He knew clearly that they would soon scatter in fear and that he would be left isolated. Yet he declared with certainty that he would not be alone, because the Father was with him. This reminds us that true presence is not a matter of how many people are around us, but of whether God is beside us.

Jesus tells us that this world is full of trouble, and believers cannot escape hardship and challenge. But he wants us to have peace in him. This peace does not mean there are no storms around us. It means that our hearts are strong and steady because we are joined to Christ.

Our final hope is that Jesus has overcome. Through the cross and resurrection he conquered sin, death, and the powers of the world. When we trust in him, we can live in this world as victors, no longer held by fear, facing the future with strong faith.
a: Be Sure of God’s Presence
Even when you are alone or abandoned, believe that the Father is with you.
Look for Peace in Christ
Do not expect a life without trouble. Find true rest by staying connected to the Lord.
Live as a Victor
Whatever your circumstances, remember that Christ has overcome the world, and through him we too can have victory.
q: When I face trouble or loneliness, do I look more at my circumstances, or at the truth that Christ has already overcome?
pr: Lord, thank You for promising Your presence and Your peace. Even in trouble and loneliness, You are with me. Strengthen my heart so that I have peace in You and stand firm in the truth that You have overcome. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: In Christ I have peace, for he has overcome the world!

t: Building Up the Body of Christ in Love
v: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling,
one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in us all.
He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers;
for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full grown man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,
that we may no longer be children, tossed back and forth and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in craftiness, after the wiles of error;
but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ,

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.
b: Paul reminds us that since we have been called by God, we should answer with a life worthy of that calling. This life is not about exalting ourselves but about living with humility, gentleness, and patience, bearing with one another in love. When we are joined together in peace, we keep the unity the Spirit gives, because we all belong to one body and have one Lord, one faith, and one God.

God has given different gifts and roles, not so that we compare ourselves with one another, but to equip the saints, so that each person can do their part to build up the body of Christ. This is the direction of spiritual growth: from the unsteadiness of children to mature adulthood, filled with the stature of Christ, able to tell truth from error.

The church grows not by strategy but by being joined to Christ through love for one another. When every member serves faithfully in their own place, the whole body is built up, matures in love, and brings glory to Christ the head.
a: Live Out Humility and Patience
Practice humility and gentleness in everyday life. Do not rush to argue or promote yourself, but bear with one another in love.
Find Your Role and Be Faithful
Whether teaching, serving, caring, or praying, see it as a trust from God and use your gift faithfully to build up the body.
Build Unity in Love
Learn to treat one another with honesty and love, joined together in Christ, so that the church becomes a community full of life and witness.
q: Do I value my place in the body of Christ? How can I do my part in love to build up the church?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for choosing me to be a part of Your body. Give me humility and patience so that I can bear with my brothers and sisters in love, and faithfully use the gifts You have given me in the church. May we all be united in the faith and attain to the full stature of Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will do my part in the body of Christ, and build together with every member in love!

t: Enjoying Your Portion Before God
v: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.

Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life, because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.
b: The Preacher reminds us that hoarding wealth does not secure a person’s life and may bring burden and harm. Riches can vanish in a moment through misfortune, leaving nothing for the next generation. We come naked and we go naked, and nothing we labor for can be carried away. If we chase only money, we spend our lives in darkness and fall into worry and pain.

But the Preacher also points to another way: before God, learn to take hold of today and enjoy the portion he gives. The joy found in eating, drinking, working, and daily life is a gift from God. When we understand that all of it comes from him, we are no longer bound by “how much we have,” and can simply find satisfaction in our labor.

True joy does not come from wealth itself but from God’s grace. God can fill a person’s heart with gladness, so that they are no longer tangled up over the length of life or the troubles of the world, because he himself has become the satisfaction of our hearts.
a: See the Limits of Wealth
Do not depend on money to define the worth of your life. Wealth is unreliable and cannot go with you into eternity.
Take Hold of the Day God Gives
Learn to give thanks in daily life, and see every meal and every labor as God’s grace and your portion.
Find Joy in God
Turn to God as the source of your satisfaction, trusting that he himself can make your heart glad, so that even in limited circumstances you can live abundantly.
pr: Dear Father, do not let me be bound by wealth, and do not let me be anxious over lack. Help me learn contentment and give thanks and rejoice in the portion You give. May I not rely on fleeting money but on Your eternal grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I choose to give thanks and rejoice in the portion God has given me, for he is my true satisfaction!

t: A Faith That Still Cries Out in the Darkness
v: LORD, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you.
You have laid me in the lowest pit, in the darkest depths.
Your wrath lies heavily on me. You have afflicted me with all your waves. Selah.
You have taken my friends from me. You have made me an abomination to them. I am confined, and I can’t escape.
My eyes are dim from grief. I have called on you daily, LORD. I have spread out my hands to you.
Do you show wonders to the dead? Do the departed spirits rise up and praise you? Selah.
Is your loving kindness declared in the grave? Or your faithfulness in Destruction?
Are your wonders made known in the dark? Or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
But to you, LORD, I have cried. In the morning, my prayer comes before you.
LORD, why do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me?
I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up. While I suffer your terrors, I am distracted.
Your fierce wrath has gone over me. Your terrors have cut me off.
They came around me like water all day long. They completely engulfed me.
You have put lover and friend far from me, and my friends into darkness.
b: This is a deep lament. The psalmist sets his despair, questions, and pain before God without polish. He neither hides from the darkness nor pretends to be strong. He lays his real predicament before God, crying out day and night and spreading out his hands. That honesty is itself an expression of faith: in his most helpless moment, he still cries out to the God who can save.

The passage bares the loneliness and sense of abandonment: friends have drawn away, body and spirit are pressed down, and even worship seems impossible. This reminds us that spiritual darkness is not only a matter of outward circumstances. It is also a real experience in the depths of the soul. In such a place, the psalmist’s steadfastness is not cheap optimism. He chooses to bring his doubts to the Lord who can answer, and even when no answer comes at once, he keeps asking.

Although this psalm has hardly any clear word of comfort, it teaches a spiritual lesson: in a night we cannot understand, real spiritual life is placing our pain in God’s hands and keeping the habit of crying out to him. This continued crying out entrusts our lives to the Lord who is beyond the darkness, and waits for him to bring light and salvation in his own time.
a: Admit the Darkness and Pour Out Your Heart Honestly
— When your heart is heavy or you feel abandoned, do not pretend all is well. Like the psalmist, bring your real feelings to God, crying out day and night and praying with open hands.
Keep the Habit of Prayer Even Without an Answer
— In seasons of spiritual desolation, hold all the more to morning prayer and crying out. Let prayer be your lasting connection with God, not just a tool for instant answers.
Seek Support in Relationships and Show Compassion
— When you see others swallowed by darkness, do not draw away. Offer your company and your prayers, and be a bridge for others from darkness to light.
q: In the night of my life, am I still willing to speak honestly to God and keep praying? Am I also willing to be a hand that walks with others through the darkness?
pr: Dear Father, I bring the darkness and questions in my heart to You. When I feel abandoned and trapped, hear my cry and give me strength to lift my hands to You even in the night. Send Your presence to light my darkness, and make me a vessel who can comfort and accompany others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Even in the deepest darkness, I will cry out to the God who can save me, and he will watch over me.

t: We Have a Great High Priest Who Sympathizes with Us
v: Having then a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let’s hold tightly to our confession.
For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.
Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
The high priest can deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, because he himself is also surrounded with weakness.
Because of this, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people, as well as for himself.
Nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.
So also Christ didn’t glorify himself to be made a high priest, but it was he who said to him, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father.”
As he says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”
b: This passage ties the Old Testament office of high priest to the person of Christ, so that we see his glory and grace. The old high priests had to offer sacrifices for the people and for themselves, because they too were weak and sinful. But Jesus, our high priest, is without sin and yet sympathizes with our weaknesses, because he was tempted in every way. He is not a God far above us who does not understand human struggle. He has walked our road himself and overcome sin, and he has become our perfect mediator.

So we can draw near “with boldness” to the throne of grace. Not because we are flawless, but because he has opened the way for us. He has offered himself for us as an everlasting sacrifice for sin, and he is a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. This means we can come to him at any time to receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

This is a great comfort. When we feel weak, fall, or feel unworthy, we do not need to stay away from God. We should come to him all the more boldly, for he understands us and has already prepared grace for us. His presence is more than forgiveness. It is ongoing help, so that we can walk steadily at every step of life.
a: Draw Near to God Boldly
Do not stay away from God because of failure or weakness. His throne is a place of grace, and you can return to him at any time.
Rely on His Mercy and Help
In temptation, pressure, or difficulty, do not just grit your teeth and push through. Draw on the grace he gives in time of need.
Follow His Compassion
Since we have received his sympathy, learn to understand others’ weaknesses with empathy and love, and do not judge lightly.
q: When I am weak or struggling, do I truly believe Jesus understands what I am going through? Is my first instinct to come to the throne of grace for his mercy and help?
pr: Lord, thank You for being my high priest. You understand my struggles, and You opened the way to the throne of grace for me. Help me not to pull back in failure but to come boldly to You and receive grace. Teach me Your heart, so that I may sympathize with and help others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have a high priest who sympathizes with my weakness. I will come boldly to the throne of grace, receive mercy, find grace, and be helped!

t: Who May Dwell on God’s Holy Hill?
v: LORD, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your holy hill?
He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart;
he who doesn’t slander with his tongue, nor does evil to his friend, nor casts slurs against his fellow man;
in whose eyes a vile man is despised, but who honors those who fear the LORD; he who keeps an oath even when it hurts, and doesn’t change;
he who doesn’t lend out his money for usury, nor take a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be shaken.
b: In this psalm David asks an important question: “Who shall dwell on your holy hill?” This is not only about ritual qualification but a test of character. Those who can live in God’s presence are not merely outwardly pious but truly upright within.

The people God delights in walk blamelessly, do what is right, and speak truth in their hearts. They do not profit by lies or wound with their tongues, but face people and matters with truth and righteousness. Such a life does not chase surface piety but lives out a life that fits the faith.

Such people also honor those who fear the Lord and draw a line against evil. Their promises can be trusted, even when it costs them. They keep clean in money and gain, and do not live on unrighteous profit. God promises that such people will never be shaken, because their foundation is God himself.
a: Be Honest and Upright
In public or in private, act with truth and integrity.
Use Your Words Well
Avoid criticism, judgment, and hurtful words. Learn to build others up with what you say.
Keep Your Word and Stay Clean
In promises, money, and relationships, stay pure, and do not compromise for profit or convenience.
q: Does my life reflect honesty, righteousness, and integrity? Before God, am I a person who is the same inside and out?
pr: Dear Father, You call us to be holy so that we may dwell on Your holy hill. Search me and remove falsehood and unrighteousness, and help me live with integrity and honesty. Let my promises and actions match, so that I am a person who pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will act with integrity, with heart and words in agreement, and dwell in God’s presence forever!

t: Declare His Glory Every Day
v: Oh give thanks to the LORD. Call on his name. Make what he has done known among the peoples.
Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
Seek the LORD and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
He is the LORD our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
when you were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners in it.
They went about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes,
“Don’t touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to the LORD, all the earth! Display his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, and his marvelous works among all the peoples.
b: In this song of David we are reminded that worship is not only the hymns we sing at gatherings but an attitude of life. God’s people are called to “make known what he has done among the peoples.” This is an ongoing witness, making God’s marvelous works our theme of conversation and praise. When our hearts rejoice as we seek him, our lives naturally overflow in worship.

David also reminds Israel to remember what God has done in history. Though they were few in number and sojourners in a foreign land, God himself protected them, allowed no one to oppress them, and even rebuked kings for their sake. This shows that God is the Lord who keeps his covenant and shows steadfast love, and his faithfulness goes far beyond human limits.

Finally, David’s vision does not stop with Israel but reaches the whole earth. He declares, “Sing to Yahweh, all the earth! Display his salvation from day to day.” This is a universal call to worship, inviting everyone to tell of God’s glory and wonders. True worship is not limited to one people but extends to all nations.
a: Make Thanksgiving a Daily Attitude
Spend time each day thanking God for his works, and share his grace as your testimony.
Remember God’s Faithfulness
Do not forget his past guidance and protection. This is the foundation of our faith for the future.
Live a Life That Proclaims
Do not worship only at gatherings, but tell of his glory and salvation in daily life.
q: Does my worship stop at the gathering? Am I willing to proclaim his glory every day, in word and deed?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for Your marvelous works and faithful guidance. Help me always remember Your grace, and tell others of Your glory and salvation in my daily life. May my life be a song of praise to You, so that all peoples see Your glory through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will proclaim God’s salvation every day and tell of his glory to the ends of the earth!

t: Two Are Better Than One
v: There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then do I labor and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
b: The Preacher points out that a person who toils alone, only for wealth and achievement, with no one to share it with, is not only empty but burdened with misery. If wealth cannot bring the satisfaction of relationships, in the end it is only vanity.
On the contrary, God designed us to live in community.
“Two are better than one,” because working together yields a richer reward. The support and companionship found in relationships is far steadier and happier than fighting alone.

If one falls, a companion can lift him up. But if he is alone, no one will help him up, and that is a dangerous place to be. This reminds us that the worth of life does not lie in fighting alone, but in walking with others, supporting one another, and walking in the way that pleases God.
a: Stop Fighting Alone
Do not chase only wealth or achievement while neglecting real relationships with people.
Learn to Support One Another
Among friends, family, or in a small group, take the initiative to be someone who supports others.
Treasure Spiritual Companions
On the road of faith, walk together with brothers and sisters so that your life is made stronger.
q: Do I often center my life on labor and achievement and neglect the importance of walking with others? Am I willing to be a companion who lifts others when they fall?
pr: Dear Father, You know that people were not meant to live alone. Help me leave behind the emptiness of lonely toil, learn to walk with others, and support one another. May my life no longer be only for myself, but together with others bear good fruit. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will treasure my companions on the way and live a life of supporting one another!

t: Walking in the Light, Sins Forgiven
v: This is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie and don’t tell the truth.
But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin.
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
b: The apostle John declares plainly that “God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.” This means that God’s nature is perfectly holy, righteous, and true, and allows no falseness or hiding. If we claim to have fellowship with God yet choose to walk in darkness, we deceive ourselves and are not living in the truth.

To truly walk with God is to choose to walk in the light. This means not only living honestly and openly, but being willing to let the light expose our weaknesses and impurities. When we live in the light, our relationships with one another are built on sincerity, and at the same time the blood of Jesus cleanses us so that we can stand clean before God.

But if a person thinks they have no sin, they cannot experience forgiveness. Only by confessing our sins, and relying on God’s faithful and righteous character, will he forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness. This is God’s promise, and it is the key to our freedom.
a: Choose a Life in the Light
Do not hide your sin and weakness. Be brave and live in the light of God.
Fellowship Sincerely with One Another
Be real among the members, without falseness or cover-up, and let love and trust be the foundation that joins you.
Confess and Repent Often
Humbly admit your wrongs, receive the cleansing of the blood of Jesus, and gain freedom and joy in your heart.
q: Is there something in which I still live in darkness and am unwilling to let God’s light shine? Do I confess often and let the blood of Jesus cleanse me?
pr: Dear Father, You are light, and in You is no darkness at all. Shine on me and remove the hidden sin and falseness in my heart, so that I may truly walk in the light. Thank You for forgiving me through the blood of Jesus and cleansing me from all unrighteousness. May my life be free in the light and in true fellowship with You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will walk in the light, cleansed by the blood of Jesus, and live in truth and freedom!

t: Let the Word Become the Voice of Life
v: Let my cry come before you, LORD. Give me understanding according to your word.
Let my supplication come before you. Deliver me according to your word.
Let my lips utter praise, for you teach me your statutes.
Let my tongue sing of your word, for all your commandments are righteousness.
Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.
I have longed for your salvation, LORD. Your law is my delight.
Let my soul live, that I may praise you. Let your ordinances help me.
I have gone astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I don’t forget your commandments.
b: The psalmist closes with an urgent plea, setting all his hopes and troubles in the light of God’s word. He does not treat the word as abstract doctrine but as a living reality: it gives understanding, deliverance, praise, and help. The whole passage shows a spiritual habit: take God’s word as the standard of life, and let both the words of your mouth and the motives of your heart be shaped by Scripture.

There is also real spiritual experience here. The psalmist admits he is lost (“I have gone astray like a lost sheep”), yet he does not forget God’s commandments, and he knows he needs to be found. Salvation, wisdom, strength, and praise all come from the word. When a person chooses to delight in God’s statutes, they are helped in weakness and renewed by the word, so that their life continues and gives glory to God.

One simple practical point: connect your daily cries and reflection to sentences of Scripture. Let prayer be not vague wishes but words carrying the weight and direction of Scripture, so that God’s word becomes the compass of your heart and the strength of your daily life.
a: Begin Each Day’s Prayer with Scripture
— Each day choose one verse, read it, then turn it into your own prayer, asking God for understanding and help.
Let the Word Shape Your Praise and Speech
— Before you speak, let the truth of Scripture adjust your tone and content, so that your praise is deepened by truth.
Ask God to Find You When You Are Lost
— When you feel lost or have fallen, cry out at once with a familiar verse, relying on God’s promise and not on your own strength.
q: Which verse will I use as my cry today? Am I willing to let Scripture be my first source of prayer and comfort?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for guiding us with Your word. I admit I often need Your understanding and deliverance. Help me with Your precepts, so that my mouth can offer praise that pleases You. When I am lost, seek me, and sustain me according to Your word, so that my life is kept alive by You and glorifies You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I take God’s word as the light of my life; he will lead me home and give me strength!

t: Genuine Love in Everyday Life
v: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor that which is evil. Cling to that which is good.
In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor prefer one another,
not lagging in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord,
rejoicing in hope, enduring in troubles, continuing steadfastly in prayer,
contributing to the needs of the saints, and given to hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don’t curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Don’t be wise in your own conceits.
b: Here Paul paints a “real-life picture of Christian living.” First he reminds us that love must not be hypocritical. Love is not surface politeness but sincere and pure. It hates evil and eagerly holds to what is good. True love has both principle and warmth.

He goes on to say that love begins with those closest to us, the members of the body, with tender affection and honoring one another. At the same time, we serve the Lord with a fervent spirit. Such a life is diligent, not lazy; passionate, not cold.

For different situations Paul gives three attitudes: rejoice in hope, endure in suffering, and continue steadfastly in prayer. This frame of mind lets believers stand firm even in adversity. He also calls us to care for practical needs, to share with those who lack and show hospitality to strangers, and even in persecution to bless instead of curse. This is a high training in love.

Finally, he reminds us to be of the same mind with others, to rejoice and weep with them, not to be proud, and to be willing to accept the humble. This way of life is living out the love of Christ, and it is the true witness of the church.
a: Love Sincerely
Learn to hate evil and cling to good, so that love is not only on the lips but an action from the heart.
Serve with Fervor
In serving God and people, do not be lazy or passive. Hold on to your passion.
Live in Unity
Rejoice and weep with others, humbly accept the lowly, and build relationships of one mind.
q: Is my love sincere and principled? In service and relationships, do I show the humility and fervor of Christ?
pr: Dear Father, put sincere love in my heart, so that I hate what is evil and cling to what is good. Help me serve You fervently and love people diligently. Teach me to be of one mind with others, to accept them humbly, and in trouble to still hold on to joy and patience. May my life be a witness to Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will live out sincere love, serve the Lord with fervor, and build others up with humility!
